q.t: How many lines does guitar TAB have?
q.e: One line for each of the six strings.

q.t: In TAB, the top line is…
q.e: TAB puts the highest-sounding string on top.

q.t: In TAB, what does a number on a line mean?
q.e: The number is the fret on that string.

q.t: In TAB, what does 0 mean?
q.e: 0 = no fret pressed — the open string.

q.t: Which way do you read TAB?
q.e: Like a sentence: left to right.

q.t: Two numbers stacked straight on top of each other mean…
o: play them at the same time
q.e: Stacked notes are played together — that is how TAB shows a chord.

q.t: In a chord box, an x above a string means…
q.e: x = don't play. o = play it open.

q.t: In a chord box, an o above a string means…
q.e: o = open: play the string with no finger on it.

q.t: In a chord box, a number on a dot means…
q.e: In chord boxes the number is a finger (1 index … 4 little). The fret is shown by the row.

q.t: What does TAB not show?
q.e: TAB shows where, not how long. Listen to the song to get the rhythm.

q.t: In TAB, what does 5h7 mean?
o: Pick fret 5, then hammer onto fret 7
Pick fret 7, then pull off to fret 5
q.e: h = hammer-on: pick the first note, then slam a finger onto the higher fret without picking again.

q.t: In TAB, what does 7p5 mean?
o: Pick fret 7, then pull off to fret 5
Pick fret 5, then hammer onto fret 7
q.e: p = pull-off: pick the higher note, then flick that finger off so the lower note sounds.

q.t: In TAB, 5/7 means…
o: slide from fret 5 up to fret 7
q.e: / = slide up without lifting the finger.

q.t: What does PM mean in TAB?
q.e: Rest the side of the picking hand on the strings near the bridge for a short, chunky sound.

q.t: In a chord box, which side is the thick low E string?
q.e: The chord box is the neck standing up and facing you, so the thick string is on the left.

q.t: In a chord box, the thick line across the top is…
q.e: The thick line is the nut, the top end of the neck.

q.t: In TAB a '2' means fret 2. In a chord box a '2' means…
q.e: This is the big mix-up: in a chord box the number is the finger.

q.t:
In this TAB, which string is played?
e|-----|
B|--3--|
G|-----|
q.e: The 3 is on the B line, so play the B string at fret 3.

q.t: In the Em chord, which strings have fingers on them?
q.e: Em: fret 2 on the A string (finger 2) and fret 2 on the D string (finger 3). Everything else is open.

q.t: Why does TAB put the high e string on the top line?
o: Higher notes go higher on the page
q.e: Like all written music, TAB puts higher-sounding notes higher up.

q.t:
Which note does this play?
e|-----|
B|--1--|
q.e: B string fret 1: B → C.

q.t:
Which note does this play?
e|--3--|
B|-----|
q.e: High e fret 3: E → F (1) → F♯ (2) → G (3).

q.t:
Which note does this play?
G|--2--|
D|-----|
q.e: G string fret 2: G → G♯ → A.

q.t: What notes does B|-1-3-| then e|-0-| play?
q.e: B fret 1 = C, B fret 3 = D, open high e = E.

q.t: Am in a chord box: x o (fret 2: finger 2 on D, finger 3 on G) (fret 1: finger 1 on B) o. Which string is not played?
q.e: The x is over the low E, so strum from the A string down.

q.t: In the Am chord, finger 1 goes on…
q.e: Am: finger 1 on B fret 1, finger 2 on D fret 2, finger 3 on G fret 2.

q.t: Em written as TAB, from low E to high e, is…
q.e: Low E open, A fret 2, D fret 2, then G, B and e open.

q.t: Am written as TAB, from low E to high e, is…
q.e: Low E not played, A open, D fret 2, G fret 2, B fret 1, high e open.

q.t: Why can't you learn a song's rhythm from TAB alone?
o: TAB shows where notes are, not how long
TAB has no numbers for open strings
TAB is read right to left
q.e: TAB gives string and fret, but not note lengths — listen to the song for that.

q.t: Why is the chord box drawn with the thick string on the left?
o: It's how the neck looks held upright facing you
Because thick strings are played first
q.e: Hold the guitar up with the neck pointing at the ceiling: the thick string is on your left.

q.t: Which TAB shows the open low E and open A played together?
o: A on fret 0 directly above E on fret 0
E on fret 0, then A on fret 0 to its right
Two zeros side by side on the E line
A 0 on the high e and a 0 on the B
q.e: Notes played together are stacked straight up and down.

q.t: This TAB: B|-3-1-| after e|-0-|. What notes, in order?
q.e: Open e = E, B fret 3 = D, B fret 1 = C. That is the start of Hot Cross Buns.

q.t: In G|-0-0-| then B|-3-3-|, what are the notes?
q.e: Open G = G. B fret 3: B → C → C♯ → D. That is the start of Twinkle Twinkle.

q.t: A chord box shows a dot with '3' in the fret-2 row on the D string. What do you do?
o: Ring finger on the D string, fret 2
Ring finger on the D string, fret 3
Middle finger on the D string, fret 3
q.e: The number is the finger (3 = ring). The row tells you the fret (2).

q.t: What is the difference between a hammer-on and a slide?
o: A hammer-on drops a new finger; a slide moves the same finger
A hammer-on goes down; a slide goes up
A slide needs a new pick stroke
q.e: Hammer-on: a second finger comes down. Slide: one finger keeps pressing and travels along the string.

q.t: Why does a pull-off make the lower note sound without picking?
o: Flicking the finger off plucks the string
The lower note was already ringing loudly
q.e: As the finger leaves, it catches the string slightly — that flick is a tiny pluck, so the note below sounds.

q.t: A TAB line reads A|-3-| and E|-3-| stacked. Which notes sound together?
q.e: A fret 3: A → A♯ → B → C. Low E fret 3: E → F → F♯ → G. So C and G together.

q.t: Which TAB line plays the notes A – B – C going up on one string?
q.e: A string: open = A, fret 2 = B (a whole step), fret 3 = C (B→C is a half step).

q.t: In a chord box, a dot is in the fret-1 row but there is no number in it. What does that tell you?
o: Which fret and string, but not which finger
Which finger, but not which fret
q.e: The position of the dot shows the string and fret. The number, when given, is the finger — without it, choose the comfortable one.

q.t: You see a 2 on a line. How do you know whether it means fret 2 or finger 2?
q.e: In TAB, numbers are frets. In a chord box, numbers are fingers — the box's rows show the frets.
